title: Plain simulation of an oracle computation
statement: Let $M$ be a finite oracle Turing machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes over the binary alphabet, let $D$ be a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet, and let $O$ be a language of binary strings. Let $\tau:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ be nondecreasing, and suppose $D$ decides $O$ within time $\tau$. Then there exist a finite Turing machine $P$ over the binary alphabet and a natural number $a$ such that $P$ has at least $k+1$ work tapes and the following holds: for every binary input $x$, every family $w$ of $k+1$ binary words whose last word is empty, and every $t\in\mathbb{N}$, if the run of $M$ with oracle $O$, started on $x$ in its initial state with the words $w$ on its $k+1$ work tapes, empty output, and all work-tape heads at the origin, has halted after $t$ steps, then there is an $s\le a(t+1)(t+1+\tau(t))$ such that $P$, started on $x$ in its initial state with the first $P$ work-tape words of $w$, empty output, and all work-tape heads at the origin, has halted after $s$ steps and has the same output as the run of $M$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite oracle Turing machine over the binary alphabet, with $k$ ordinary work tapes
$D$ is a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet
$O$ is a language of binary strings
The last word of the supplied family of $k+1$ words is empty
The oracle run from the specified tape-word configuration halts after $t$ steps
